texts: doha about finally giving up and just falling at the Lord's feet
After ten years of trying to fix my life by clever plans and hard bargaining, I finally told God quietly that I have no more schemes left and I am simply His.
refuge, Lord's feet
I would like a doha about a proud and clever man who has tried everything to save himself, and who at last lays down all his cleverness and effort and takes shelter at the Lord's feet, empty-handed.
I lay my cleverness at Your feet like a worn-out garment, Beloved; clothe me now in Your shelter.
O Lord, I have no strength left to carry my own name; at Your feet I lay it down.
doha on surrender - dropping all my own effort and trusting the Lord
When my business collapsed and every plan I made failed, I sat down in the dark and finally said, You decide, I am done deciding.
Compose a doha about letting go of all one's own scheming and striving, and placing oneself completely at the Lord's feet, saying: I am Yours, do with me what You will.
empty hands, Lord's feet
The cleric told me I must earn God's favour with a thousand rules, but sitting alone in a cage of my own anxieties I decided to just give myself up and say, Take me as I am.
Write a doha about a cleric who binds men with endless rules, and a soul in a cage who ignores them all and simply falls at the Lord's feet, surrendering everything it has and hopes for.
Caged by my own cleverness, I fold my wings at the cleric's useless rules and at Your feet; open, or do not open, as You wish.
cleric, cage, surrender
doha with a cleric and a cage about giving up and surrendering to the Lord
lamp and palace doha - leaving everything and taking refuge in the Lord
lamp, palace, Lord's refuge
My father walked out of his palace-like office tower one evening, left the lamp on his desk burning, and said he was going to rest at God's feet, and never came back to that life.
The palace blazes with a thousand lamps, yet the soul finds true shelter only at the quiet feet of the Lord.
Please write a doha about a ruler who leaves his palace and his lamp-lit throne, and sits down at the feet of the Lord with nothing, having realised no cleverness of his own ever protected him.
beggar, well, at Your feet
I used to think I could pull myself out of every hole with my own skill, but sitting by the water well like a beggar, I finally admitted I need God to hold me up.
I came to the well as a beggar with an empty pot, Lord, and I lay my cleverness at Your feet.
Compose a doha about a beggar sitting by a water well who has given up all his own cleverness and effort, and waits, with nothing, at the Lord's feet for whatever the Lord chooses to give.
beggar and well doha - give up your own effort and rely on the Lord
I want a doha about the moment when the seeker stops trying to be clever and strong and simply says, Lord, I am Yours; the burden of my life is Yours now, and I rest at Your feet.
I have stopped rowing against the current; take the oar from my hand, O Lord, for I am Yours.
surrender, nothing left
After exhausting myself trying to control everything at work and at home, I took one deep breath and decided that for once I would stop controlling and trust.
doha about giving up control and trusting God completely
The old mirror in my hallway showed a tired man who had spent his life being clever, and that morning I knelt and said, I cannot do this alone any more.
The mirror shows a proud face; the Lord's feet show the humble one that has learned to bow.
mirror, humble surrender
mirror doha about giving up my own cleverness and bowing to the Lord
Please write a doha about a man who looks into a mirror and sees a lifetime of cleverness and self-reliance, then bows down at the Lord's feet and gives up the figure he has been defending.
taking shelter in God
Not by cunning, not by strength, but by laying down my head at Your feet, O Lord, am I saved.
doha: leave everything and take refuge in the Lord
Compose a doha for a person who has tried every path and every clever trick and still feels lost; tell him to take refuge at the Lord's feet and give up the trying, for the Lord will carry him.
After my third failed attempt to rebuild my life, I stopped listing plans and simply sat in silence, hands open, saying that I would let Him lead.
My daughter was born with a pearl-white face under the full moon, and in that moment I knew all my planning was pointless and I could only offer her, and myself, up to God.
doha with a pearl and the moon, about surrendering at the Lord's feet
Write a doha about a pearl in the deep and the moon in the sky, neither of which arranges its own fate, and the soul that learns from them to give up its effort and rest at the Lord's feet.
The moon does not climb the sky by effort, nor the pearl form by will; so I give myself up to Your feet.
pearl, moon, surrender to God
touchstone, dew, taking refuge
touchstone and dew doha, give up and hand it all to the Lord

Please write a doha about the touchstone that tests the soul and the dew that vanishes at dawn, saying that the clever and the strong both fall short in the end, and only yielding at the Lord's feet lasts.
Facing my own tests of life one after another, like metal on a touchstone, I woke at dawn with dew on the grass and simply asked God to take over.
The touchstone tests my cleverness and finds it hollow as dew; only the Lord's feet hold the one who surrenders.
surrender doha: I give up, Lord, you handle it
After years of fighting a long illness with every remedy I could find, I woke one morning and told the doctors and my family that I would trust whatever happens.
Please write a doha about the peace that comes when one gives up the endless planning and struggling of the clever mind and simply places oneself at the Lord's feet, trusting whatever may come.
The struggling oar falls from my hand and I drift in Your mercy, O Lord, content to be carried.
giving up, trusting God
Write a doha about a woman standing at a closed door with a pearl in her hand, who stops trying every clever way to get in and simply sits at the Lord's feet to wait for Him to open it.
I knock at no door now, I bargain with no pearl; I lie at Your feet and wait.
door, pearl, take refuge
I spent years trying every clever way to get a promotion at the firm, even buying a rare pearl for the boss, until one night I stood at a closed door and told God, I am done, You decide.
doha with a door and a pearl about surrendering to the Lord
The sun rises without being asked and sets without being told; so I too lay my will at Your feet.
sun, resting in the Lord

Compose a doha about the sun that rises and sets without any effort of its own, saying that a soul should likewise stop striving in its own cleverness and rest at the Lord's feet, trusting His will completely.
doha: the sun does its thing, I should just surrender to God too
One bad morning I watched the sun rise on its own and thought: it never plans or worries; I should give up my own endless planning and trust God the same way.
Between caring for a sick child and the bees buzzing over our balcony garden, I broke down and simply handed my worries over to God, thread by thread.
Please write a doha about a bee that works hard but cannot control the thread of its fate, saying the wise soul stops trying to control everything and lays itself down at the Lord's feet.
doha with thread and a bee about surrendering to God
A bee circles, a thread unravels, and the weary soul at last falls silent at the Lord's feet.
thread, bee, give up, surrender
surrender at the Lord's feet
doha - I give up all my cleverness, Lord, I'm Yours
After a lifetime of winning arguments, I lost the last one with my wife, and instead of fighting back I sat down and quietly gave all of it up to God.
I would like a doha for a proud scholar who has argued, calculated and planned all his life, and who at last lays down every clever argument and takes shelter at the Lord's feet like a child.
Cleverness is a heavy cloak; I drop it at Your feet, Beloved, and shiver gladly in Your mercy.
The yogi's hard postures have not freed him; only the Lord's feet shelter one who lets go of his own strength.
yogi doha - all that yoga effort fails, just fall at God's feet
Write a doha about a yogi who has mastered every posture and breath, yet remains restless until he drops all his cleverness and effort and takes refuge at the Lord's feet like a helpless child.
My uncle trained as a yogi for twenty years and mastered every difficult technique, but on his deathbed he said he had nothing left to offer but his helplessness.
yogi, Lord's shelter
Not in the temple's carved halls but at Your feet, O Lord, where I lay down every clever thing I know.
temple, taking refuge
I went to the temple every week with expensive offerings, hoping to buy God's attention, until one day I walked in empty-handed and just stood there, finished with bargaining.
Please write a doha about a man who brings a thousand clever offerings to the temple and gains nothing, until he comes empty-handed and gives up everything, even his pride, at the Lord's feet.
temple doha - quit bargaining with God and just give yourself over to Him
at Your feet, Lord
Having failed the exam three times despite every study trick I knew, I closed my books the night before and just asked God to do with me what He liked.
I would like a doha for a person worn out by trying to solve everything by his own cleverness, telling him that peace comes only when he gives up the effort and rests in the Lord's care.
Cleverness fails, strength falters, and the tired heart finds its rest only in the shelter of the Lord.
doha: I give up trying, Lord, just take care of me
The priest recites a thousand verses; I have only my empty hands and my bowed head at Your feet.
Write a doha about a priest who knows every verse and ritual but cannot save himself, while the simple soul with nothing but a bowed head and open hands finds refuge at the Lord's feet.
The priest in our village teaches long complicated rituals, but my grandmother just lies down each night and says that she hands everything to God.
priest, taking refuge
priest doha - forget the rituals, just give yourself to the Lord
Write a doha about a bier carried through the streets and a caged bird behind bars, both utterly helpless, showing that the only wise thing is to lay yourself at the Lord's feet before the end.
bier, cage, helpless, Lord
bier and cage doha about giving up and relying wholly on God
Sitting beside my father's bier I felt as helpless as a caged bird, with no clever plan left, and I could only whisper to God that I was in His hands.
Bier and cage, both hold the helpless; only the Lord's feet give the soul a place to rest.
cage doha: I have no tricks left, Lord, take me in
cage, Lord's refuge
Compose a doha about a bird in a cage that has stopped beating its wings against the bars and now rests quietly, giving itself up to whatever the Lord wills, finding peace at last.
After struggling for months in a job that felt like a cage, I stopped hunting for escape routes and simply asked God to place me where He wished.
The bird in the cage ceases to beat its wings and sings of the Lord, whose will is the only sky.
palace and tortoise doha - drawing in and taking refuge in the Lord
The palace crumbles, the tortoise draws in its limbs; the wise soul folds all its cleverness at the Lord's feet.
Please write a doha about a tortoise that draws all its limbs into its shell for safety, as the soul should draw in all its scattered cleverness and rest at the Lord's feet, not in any palace.
My boss lives in a mansion and trusts only his own tricks, while I, slow as a tortoise near the palace gate, have learned to lean on God and sleep soundly.
palace, tortoise, Lord's shelter
When the strength of my arms is spent and my wit has run dry, I fall at Your feet and am held.
short doha on putting my whole trust in the Lord after trying everything
My marriage was falling apart, and after trying every strategy and therapist, I finally went quiet and said, God, I place it all in Your hands.
Please write a doha for the soul that has exhausted its wit and strength and now bows its head at the Lord's feet, trusting that He will do what it could never do for itself.
refuge in the Lord
At my grandfather's bier, the family argued over arrangements, but my grandmother simply folded her hands and said everything is now in God's hands.
At the bier all cleverness falls silent; only the Lord's feet remain as shelter for the one who lets go.
doha plz with a bier, give it all to the Lord
Compose a doha beside a bier where the mourners finally understand that no plan or cleverness could have saved the one they loved, and that all they can do is give themselves over to the Lord.
bier, Lord's feet
A thorn in my foot and a fish dinner that went wrong the same week made me laugh and tell God I was done managing the details of my own life.
thorn, fish, Lord's refuge
thorn and fish doha about trusting everything to God
The fish does not choose the current, the thorn does not choose its place, and I choose only to rest at Your feet.
Write a doha about a fish swept along by the current and a thorn that pricks whatever touches it, both helpless to choose their fate, and the soul that finds peace by lying at the Lord's feet.
In the mirror I saw my tired cleverness; at Your feet, I saw my freedom, Beloved.
I caught my own tired face in the mirror one morning and realised how long I had been fighting alone, and quietly turned my worries over to God.
mirror doha - I stop trying, Lord, You carry me now
Compose a doha about a person who looks in a mirror and sees only cleverness and effort, and then bows down at the Lord's feet, giving up the proud image of himself that he has defended for years.
mirror, falling at Your feet
Neither mosque nor forest holds the answer; at Your feet alone does the tired soul find shelter.
doha with a mosque and a forest, about giving up and falling at God's feet
Write a doha about a man who seeks peace in a mosque and in the depths of a forest, with every clever technique he knows, until he lays all his effort down and finds refuge at the Lord's feet.
I tried praying at the mosque, then retreating into the forest for weeks, trying every method; in the end I simply gave myself up to God's will in the quiet.
mosque, forest, taking refuge
Please write a doha about a heavy stone and a tortoise, the one too hard to move and the other too slow, showing that effort is useless and the soul must rest at the Lord's feet for help.
stone and tortoise doha - give up trying, trust the Lord
I sat on a stone in the garden watching a tortoise inch along, and realised that I had been pushing and rushing all my life, and that it was time to trust God.
stone, tortoise, Lord's shelter
The stone is heavy, the tortoise slow, and I am both; carry me, Lord, for I cannot walk alone.
Lord's feet, nothing else
I would like a doha that says the clever man and the strong man both come in the end to the same place, the feet of the Lord, where all striving is laid down and the soul is sheltered.
After a lifetime of success in the city, I retired to a quiet village and found myself just sitting, hands empty, finally leaving my fate to God.
doha about giving up your own cleverness and relying on the Lord
Every road of my cleverness ended in a wall; Your feet, Lord, were the only road left.
market, washerman, taking refuge
doha with a market and a washerman about leaving all your effort to the Lord
Write a doha about a washerman who works from dawn in the market, scrubbing and bargaining with all his skill, until one day he puts down his bundle and rests at the Lord's feet, unburdened.
In the market the washerman struggles and haggles, but at the Lord's feet his bundle is set down at last.
The washerman in our market works from dawn to night haggling over every coin, but on festival evenings he sits very still and tells God he has no more tricks.
touchstone doha about giving up all cleverness and falling at the Lord's feet
The touchstone tests every claim of cleverness, and finds the soul's only worth is the bowed head at Your feet.
Please write a doha about a touchstone that tests all the clever claims of the proud, and finds that only the soul that gives up its pride and effort and rests at the Lord's feet is true.
touchstone, Lord's refuge
After the audit tested every figure I had claimed at work like a touchstone, I felt stripped of all my cleverness, and I turned to God as if for the first time.
Compose a doha about a cuckoo that sings from its branch and an elephant that stands in strength, both of which have only the Lord to depend on, as should the proud soul that gives up its cleverness.
My neighbour is huge and proud like an elephant and bragged about managing everything himself, until he lost his job and sat quietly listening to the cuckoo, asking God for help.
The cuckoo sings, the elephant tires, and both rest at the Lord's feet when the day is done.
cuckoo, elephant, Lord's refuge
cuckoo and elephant doha - give up the ego and rely on God
fish and salt doha - leaving everything to the Lord and trusting Him
The fish does not strive for water, the salt does not strive to dissolve; so the soul, at Your feet, ceases to strive.
Write a doha about a fish in water and salt dissolving in it, neither of which struggles to become what it is, and the soul that learns from them to stop striving and rest at the Lord's feet.
At the fish counter I noticed the salt they pack with each order and thought how things dissolve without effort, and how I should stop forcing my life and hand it to God.
fish, salt, Lord's shelter
Write a doha about a philosopher's stone that turns iron to wealth, saying no clever alchemy of man can match the Lord, and the one who gives up his own effort and rests at His feet is transformed.
philosopher's stone doha - drop all my cleverness and trust the Lord
My grandfather chased the legend of the philosopher's stone all his life with experiments and plans, and in old age said the only treasure he found was trusting God.
philosopher's stone, Lord's feet
Seekers chase the philosopher's stone with a hundred schemes, but the transformation comes to the soul that bows at Your feet.
After my team won every award for cleverness and strategy, I realised on a quiet night that none of it had ever protected me, and I put myself in God's care.
Compose a doha about a person who is proud of his intelligence and ability to plan, and who comes to see that all of it was only a game, and finds safety at the Lord's feet.
Cleverness is a crumbling wall; the Lord's feet are the only ground that does not give way.
cleverness useless, trust God
doha about stopping all the scheming and just trusting the Lord
Lord's refuge, no effort
I want a doha for those who say, I will do it myself, telling them that the Lord waits for them to stop and to place themselves at His feet, because He can do what they cannot.
doha: let go and hand your life to the Lord
The hand that clings lets go, the head that boasted bows; at the Lord's feet the soul is at rest.
My little brother insisted on doing everything by himself until he tripped, and when I helped him up I thought about how we all need to ask a higher hand.
bier and bell doha - nothing but the Lord's feet remains to take refuge in
When the bell tolled for my uncle's bier, all his schemes and clever dealings fell silent, and my aunt said softly that only God's shelter remains.
bier, bell, Lord's refuge
The bell tolls over the bier, and every clever plan lies down; only the Lord's feet remain.
Write a doha about the toll of a bell over a bier, reminding the proud that their cleverness and effort will not follow them, and that the only wise act is to lay down the head at the Lord's feet.
Lord, I am Yours
doha about telling God I give up and I'm His
When my wife left, I stopped trying to win her back by clever speeches and instead lay awake telling God, quietly, that I belong to Him now.
Please write a doha in which the speaker, after exhausting every clever scheme and resource, simply says to the Lord, I am Yours, take me, and finds relief in giving up all effort.
I am Yours, Beloved, and nothing more; take the reins of my cleverness and hold them away.
Write a doha about a pearl in the deep sea and a bridge over a chasm, neither made by its own cleverness, and say that the soul should rest at the Lord's feet as the bridge rests on its banks.
The pearl did not make itself, the bridge did not raise itself; so the soul rests at Your feet and is carried.
pearl and bridge doha about giving up control and trusting the Lord
pearl, bridge, Lord's refuge
Crossing the old bridge to my sister's wedding with a pearl necklace in my bag, I felt all my worries about the future fall away, and silently put myself in God's hands.
mountain, cloth sheet, Lord's feet
We climbed the mountain with a single cloth sheet between us for the night, and in the cold I stopped planning and just trusted God to get us through.
On the mountain's shoulder, wrapped in a thin cloth sheet, I give my fate to Your feet.
Compose a doha about a pilgrim on a mountain with only a thin cloth sheet to cover him, who has no cleverness or strength left and lays himself at the Lord's feet to be sheltered.
mountain and cloth sheet doha about giving up everything to the Lord
When the mosque in our neighbourhood was crowded on the last night of the fast, I stood at the edge and, instead of reciting, simply told God I could do no more.
doha with a mosque, relying wholly on the Lord and not on my own tricks
Let the mosque echo with grand speeches; I will sit quietly at Your feet, Beloved, with nothing in my hands.
mosque, Lord's refuge

Please write a doha about a man at a mosque who has recited every verse and followed every rule with great cleverness, yet finds peace only when he bows with empty hands and gives himself to the Lord.
bridge, Lord's feet
I want a doha about a bridge that cannot be crossed by cleverness or strength, for the far bank is the Lord's, and the soul can only cross by giving up its effort and resting at His feet.
bridge doha - I can't cross on my own, Lord, carry me
The old bridge in our town washed away in the monsoon, and watching helpless on the bank I felt the plain truth that I need something greater to carry me.
No bridge of my own cleverness spans this gulf; carry me over, O Lord, on Your mercy.
Lay down the load of cleverness, tired traveller of the heart; the Lord's feet are soft, and they are near.
Please write a doha for someone exhausted by years of self-reliance, telling them that the Lord's shelter is always open, and that the moment they give up their own cleverness they will find rest.
After years of being the one who solved everyone's problems, I broke down in the car park and heard myself say that I could not carry it any more, and gave it to God.
rest at the Lord's feet
doha: stop relying on yourself, rely on the Lord
My mother raised four children alone with every clever trick she knew, and when we were grown she said her whole life was only possible because she kept handing it to God.
handing everything to God
doha: I place myself in the Lord's hands, no more schemes
My plans were water, my tricks were smoke; the Lord's feet are all that remain.
Compose a doha for a person who once believed his own cleverness could win everything, but now places his whole life in the Lord's keeping and finds a peace that no scheme ever gave him.
lamp, Lord's refuge
Write a doha about a lamp that cannot light itself and a soul that cannot save itself, both depending wholly on the Lord, and the peace that comes when the soul gives up effort and rests at His feet.
On Diwali night I set a lamp on the ledge and watched it flicker, and thought of how little control I really have over anything, and quietly asked God to keep me.
lamp doha about giving up all effort and trusting the Lord
The lamp does not light itself, the soul does not save itself; both wait at the Lord's feet.
Please write a doha about a pearl that rests inside its shell, protected without its own effort, saying the soul too should stop striving and rest inside the Lord's shelter, trusting Him alone.
The pearl rests in its shell untroubled; so the soul rests in the Lord's keeping, having given up its plans.
pearl, taking refuge
pearl doha - trusting God completely instead of my own plans
I bought a pearl ring for my daughter's wedding after months of financial scheming, and on the day itself I finally put the whole outcome in God's hands.
Write a doha about a weaver at his loom, working milk-white cloth day and night with all his skill, who finally leaves it unfinished, folds his hands and rests at the Lord's feet.
My uncle weaves at his loom and drinks his milk every dawn, working all day with great skill, but on the weekly rest day he leaves everything to God and sits in silence.
The weaver leaves the loom, the milk grows cold, and he bows his head at the Lord's feet.
doha with a weaver's loom and milk, leaving it all to the Lord
loom, milk, Lord's refuge
I need a doha for a person who plans and schemes constantly out of fear, telling him that the Lord is waiting for him to give up the effort and rest in His care, where no scheme is needed.
Fear built my plans and fear tore them down; at the Lord's feet there is nothing left to fear.
I used to lie awake at night making plans for every possible disaster, until my doctor told me to stop, and I started quietly leaving it to God.
refuge in the Lord
doha for anxious people: let go and trust the Lord
Write a doha about a bitter gourd that grows sweet only when it is left to the Lord's will, saying the soul too, bitter with its own cleverness, becomes sweet when it rests at the Lord's feet.
My mother-in-law cooks bitter gourd every week and complains she cannot change its taste, and I thought: some things only God can change, and I should stop trying.
The gourd stays bitter whatever I do; only the Lord's touch can sweeten what I cannot.
bitter gourd, Lord's refuge
bitter gourd doha - trusting the Lord to change what I can't
doha about giving yourself up to God completely and finding peace
I have spent my whole career winning, and on the day I retired I walked out into the evening air and told God that from now on I would only follow.
Lord's feet, nothing more
Please write a doha about the peace that comes at the very end of all searching and trying, when the clever soul finally lays down its pride and effort and takes refuge at the Lord's feet.
After all the roads and all the wit, the soul comes to Your feet and finds it was the only place it ever wanted.
